chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a slave-girl who had been Christian, then accepted Islam and bore a child to her master. Then her master died and made a bequest concerning her emancipation as an umm walad during the time of 'Umar. Then she married a Christian monk-like man and became Christian again, and bore him two children and became pregnant with a third.

He said: He ruled that Islam should be presented to her, so it was presented to her, but she refused. Then he said: The children she bore as Christian children are slaves belonging to their brother, the one she bore to her first master; and I will imprison her until she delivers the child that is in her womb, and when she delivers, I will kill her.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This ruling is restricted to the specific case that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام explained, and it is not extended to other than it. For it is not impossible that he عليه السلام considered killing her to be in the public interest because of her apostasy and marriage, and perhaps she had married a Muslim and then apostasized and married again, thus deserving death for that and for her refusal to return to Islam. As for the ruling concerning the female apostate, it is that she is imprisoned forever if she does not return to Islam, according to what we have already presented in the previous narrations; and what he narrated further clarifies that.

key_terms.اَلْإِسْلَامُ: Islam, presented to her for return and acceptance
key_terms.اَلْقَتْلَ: execution or killing as mentioned in this specific ruling
key_terms.عَبِيدٌ: slaves, referring to the legal status of the children in this case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shi'i hadith on a female apostate in the case narrated from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning a specific case involving apostasy, marriage, slave status, and the legal status of children. Shaykh al-Tusi then clarifies that the severe ruling mentioned is confined to that particular case and should not be generalized, while the standing rule for a female apostate is perpetual imprisonment if she does not return to Islam.
